 Latest news The second US time change of 2026 is approaching, but millions of Americans will not need to adjust their clocks.
 StephanieFrey U.S. News Daylight Saving Time 2026: When do the clocks fall back in the U.S.?
 Corina González twitter Calum Roche twitter Update: Oct 25th, 2026 06:37 EDT Share Make us preferred on Google The second time change of 2026 in the United States is approaching , as daylight saving time will soon come to an end.
 Across most of the country, the clocks change twice a year : once when daylight saving time begins and again when it ends and standard time resumes. However, this year could be different, as a bill that would make daylight saving time permanent is under consideration.
 The date the clocks change in the United States
 The dates on which daylight saving time begins and ends in the United States vary each year. Daylight saving time begins on the second Sunday in March. In 2026, the change took place on Sunday, March 8, when the clocks moved forward by one hour.
 Daylight saving time remains in effect for eight months, until the clocks change again in November. Daylight saving time ends on the first Sunday in November , meaning the next time change in 2026 will take place on Sunday, Nov. 1 . 
 Do the clocks go forward or back in November?
 When daylight saving time ends, the country returns to standard time , so clocks must be turned back by one hour. People in areas that observe the time change will “gain” an extra hour of sleep.
 The change takes place at 2 a.m. local time , although most people will not need to do anything because electronic devices update automatically. Analog clocks and other devices that do not update automatically can be adjusted before going to bed.
 The states that do not change their clocks
 Hawaii and most of Arizona do not observe daylight saving time, so residents do not need to change their clocks. Arizona has not observed daylight saving time since 1968, although the Navajo Nation in the northeastern part of the state does follow it .
 The following US territories also do not observe daylight saving time: Puerto Rico, the US Virgin Islands, the Northern Mariana Islands, Guam and American Samoa .
 Uncertainty over the future of the US time change
 Several months ago, the US House of Representatives approved a bill that would make daylight saving time permanent nationwide , eliminating the twice-yearly clock changes.
 The proposal, which is supported by President Trump, is now awaiting approval in the Senate. If it is passed by Congress, it will then go to President Donald Trump to be signed into law.
